unit_description: This unit introduces area as the space inside a shape. Students cover figures with unit squares, count and label square units, and find area even when some squares are hidden.
unit_goals: Understand area as the space inside a shape.
Find area when some squares are hidden.
Use square units to measure area.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students explore area through unit squares, counting square units, and finding area of partially hidden shapes.

lessons.lesson_title: Area as the Space Inside a Shape
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by tracing the inside of different shapes.
lessons.concept: Area is the amount of space inside a flat shape. We measure area by counting how many unit squares fit inside the shape with no gaps or overlaps.
lessons.practice: Identify and describe area as the space inside shapes.
lessons.objective: Understand area as the space inside a shape.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by thinking about space inside.

questions.prompt: Which has more space inside: a small circle or a big square?
questions.hint: The bigger shape has more area.

questions.prompt: Area tells us the amount of what inside a shape?
questions.hint: Area is the space inside a shape.

questions.prompt: To measure area, do we count squares or lines?
questions.hint: Area is measured in square units.

learn.title: Area as the Space Inside a Shape
teaching_points: Area is the inside space of a flat shape.
Area is measured in square units.

example.equation: Count the square units inside each shape.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A shape covers 12 square units. Another covers 8 square units. Which has more area?
try_it.hint: Compare the number of square units.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Identify which shape has more area or count square units.

bigIdea.title: Area as the Space Inside a Shape
bigIdea.subtitle: Area is the space inside
bigIdea.intro: Area is the amount of flat space inside a shape. A bigger area means more space is inside. We measure it with square units.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why do we measure area with square units?

ruleCards.description: Area is the amount of two-dimensional space a shape covers.
We use unit squares to measure area.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by covering simple shapes with square tiles on a grid.
lessons.concept: To find area, cover a shape with unit squares without gaps or overlaps. Count the squares to find the total area.
lessons.practice: Cover figures with unit squares and count the area.
lessons.objective: Cover figures with unit squares to find area.

questions.prompt: How many unit squares cover a 3 by 4 rectangle?
A shape is covered by 7 unit squares. What is its area?
questions.hint: Area is the number of unit squares.

questions.prompt: Can unit squares overlap when measuring area?
questions.hint: Squares should not overlap or leave gaps.

learn.title: Cover Figures with Unit Squares
teaching_points: Use unit squares that are the same size.
Cover the shape without gaps or overlaps.
Count the squares to find the area.

example.prompt: Cover a 4 by 5 rectangle with unit squares.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Cover a 3 by 6 rectangle. What is the area?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Cover each shape with unit squares and count the area.

flashcards.title: Unit Squares
flashcards.instructions: Review covering shapes with unit squares.

bigIdea.title: Cover Figures with Unit Squares
bigIdea.subtitle: No gaps, no overlaps
bigIdea.intro: To measure area, cover the shape with unit squares. Make sure there are no gaps and no overlaps. Count the squares to get the area.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What happens if the unit squares overlap?

ruleCards.description: Each unit square has the same area.
Count how many unit squares fit inside the shape.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting square units on a grid and labeling the area.
lessons.concept: Area is written with a number and a unit label, such as square units or sq units. Count the squares carefully and write the answer with the correct label.
lessons.practice: Count square units on grids and label the area correctly.

questions.prompt: A shape covers 15 unit squares. What is its area?
A rectangle has 5 rows of 4 squares. What is the area?
How do you write area for 9 unit squares?

learn.title: Count and Label Square Units
teaching_points: Count every unit square inside the shape.
Write the number with the label.
Use square units or sq units.

example.prompt: Count and label the area of a 2 by 7 rectangle.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Count and label the area of a 4 by 4 square.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Count the square units and write the area with the correct label.

flashcards.title: Counting and Labeling Area
flashcards.instructions: Review counting and labeling square units.

bigIdea.title: Count and Label Square Units
bigIdea.subtitle: Always include the unit label
bigIdea.intro: Area is not just a number. It is a number of square units. Always write the label so others know what you measured.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why do we write square units after an area answer?

ruleCards.description: Count the number of unit squares inside the shape.
Write square units or sq units after the number.

lessons.lesson_title: Find Area When Some Squares Are Hidden
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting visible squares and predicting the hidden ones.
lessons.concept: Even when you cannot see every square, you can use the rows and columns to find the total area. Multiply the number of rows by the number of columns.
lessons.practice: Find the area of shapes when some unit squares are hidden.
lessons.objective: Find area when some squares are hidden.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has 5 rows and 7 columns. How many square units?
Only some squares of a 4 by 6 rectangle are shown. What is the total area?
A shape has 3 rows and 8 columns. What is the area?

learn.title: Find Area When Some Squares Are Hidden

example.prompt: A rectangle has 4 rows and 9 columns, but some squares are covered. What is the area?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle has 6 rows and 5 columns. Some squares are hidden. What is the total area?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Use rows and columns to find the total area even when some squares are hidden.

flashcards.title: Rows and Columns for Area
flashcards.instructions: Review finding area using rows and columns.

bigIdea.title: Find Area When Some Squares Are Hidden
bigIdea.subtitle: Use rows and columns
bigIdea.intro: Even if you cannot see all the squares, the rows and columns tell you how many there are. Multiply rows by columns to find the total area.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do rows and columns help when some squares are hidden?

ruleCards.description: Count how many rows of squares there are.
Count how many squares are in each row.
